article.summary: Aimee is a self-hosted runtime with personal memory on Server and optional shared memory on KB. who_what.text: Aimee is a self-hosted agent runtime with personal memory on Server and optional shared memory on KB. The public repository owns the generic memory SDK, host integration, packaging and provisioning; storage, retrieval policy, ontology and maintenance are in a separately maintained private bundle.

architecture.text: The public path is a generic Go memory client over the module bus, with Server and KB hosts dispatching to an implementation selected at deployment. Without a provisioned implementation, the public adapter does not attach or provide a local datastore; readiness reports missing memory and calls fail unavailable.

The public Record includes ID, scope, tier, kind, key, content, confidence, optional metadata, validity bounds, sensitivity, authorship, utility horizon and version. MemoryRecordVersion binds schema version, owner ID, record ID and record revision; it is a mutation precondition, not a serving-eligibility proof.

The public Store exposes scoped Get, Search, Put and Delete. Optional CandidateStore selects bounded candidates but does not guarantee semantic-search completeness. Private persistence schema and ranking policy are not visible in the reviewed public tree.

behavior.text: **Write.** Put is an upsert by kind/key and IDs are assigned by the canonical source. The client borrows an already admitted bus caller and does not set principal identity or apply local policy. Actual admission and persisted write semantics belong to the installed implementation.

**Update and correction.** Basic upsert is separate from conditional mutation in an extended API. The version tuple provides an owner/record/revision precondition. Documentation describes retained revisions, but implementation conflict handling is not visible here.

**Delete and retirement.** The Store has scoped Delete. Documentation says legacy memory.delete means retained retirement: invalidation makes a record unavailable for current use but does not physically delete its payload or earlier revisions. Erasure from backups and exports is not established.

**Retrieval.** Scoped Get and Search are available; an empty query lists eligible records in scope. Candidate selection is bounded and not a completeness guarantee for semantic retrieval. Selected canonical revisions must be revalidated. The private implementation determines ranking, eligibility, and retrieval quality.

**Scope isolation.** The SDK canonicalizes user, global, workspace, and project values but does not authorize access or choose defaults. Placement and admitted caller remain host decisions. Docs separate personal Server memory from explicitly selected shared KB memory; failed private lookups do not switch stores.

**Provenance and evidence.** Record versions bind owner, row, and revision; records expose authorship and metadata. The client uses an admitted caller rather than accepting identity as a record argument. Host context release and source revalidation constrain provider dispatch, but private provenance completeness and answer support cannot be established.

**Source-visible efficiency and observability.** The client defaults to a five-second module-call deadline, bounds wire requests, and distinguishes unavailable, unauthorized, and attempted-error embedding outcomes. Candidate limits and derived-store cleanup contracts are explicit. Operational docs describe missing-module readiness, logs, and a bus probe. These are not performance measurements.

metrics.evidence: Scoped retrieval and bounded candidate contracts are visible; private ranking policy and recall/abstention outcomes were not measured.
Record revisions and mutation preconditions are exposed; correction accuracy and stale-value rates were not measured.
Delete is documented as retained retirement, not physical erasure; no leakage workload was run.
Scope canonicalization and host admission boundaries are defined; no cross-scope workload was run.
Owner/record revisions and source revalidation are present; claim-support precision and citation coverage were not adjudicated.
SDK deadlines and bounded candidates are visible; no end-to-end latency distribution or write-to-recall delay was measured.
No token, dollar-cost, or storage-efficiency results were collected for this system.
Call deadlines, framing limits, candidate bounds, readiness diagnostics, and a bus probe are source-visible; none establishes runtime throughput or resource use.

limits.text: The current memory engine is delivered as a private bundle. Public code exposes contracts and host integration rather than storage internals, ranking policy, ontology, or maintenance; the review cannot establish those hidden details.

The review inspected current public docs, generic Go SDK types and contracts, unavailable adapter, and host provider-dispatch source. It did not execute Aimee, tests, or benchmarks. Unknown means not verified by this bounded public review.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No Aimee runtime, benchmark workload, or test suite was run. Project metrics, fixture, and baseline status are protocol references, not Aimee measurements.
